item.title: The Geometry of Change
item.description: When you watch relay clusters over time, the first thing that stands out is motion. Points drift, shapes shift a little, boundaries move. But distance doesn’t tell the whole story. Two clusters can travel the same amount yet experience completely different internal changes. One stays cohesive. Another stretches at the edges. A third barely moves but rotates in place. The coordinates change, but the meaning doesn’t sit in the coordinates.
